scenes.audio: Elena enrolls in life coverage through her employer. The employer or qualifying trustees hold the master contract.
scenes.label: Opening Hook
scenes.visual: A diverse trio sits at a dark wood table in a sunlit modern office. A Hispanic woman (~40, olive skin, long dark hair, olive blouse) and a Black man (~40, dark skin, beard, grey suit) review a document. A Caucasian woman (~40, blonde hair, navy dress) observes. High-key natural lighting from large windows. Shallow depth of field.

scenes.audio: Elena receives a certificate explaining her individual protection and rights.
scenes.label: Product Information
scenes.visual: Minimalist graphic on cream background. A green box labeled '01' contains 'Master policyholder'. A green arrow points right. Clean, sans-serif typography. Static frame.

scenes.audio: The group policyholder, insured employee, and beneficiary perform different roles. An employer group covers eligible employees or defined classes under the policy.
scenes.label: Product Information
scenes.visual: Graphic adds '02 Insured member' in a dark teal box and '03 Certificate' in a white box. Teal and green accents throughout. Static camera.

scenes.audio: A labor union can instead hold coverage for eligible members. Maryland's rules for these arrangements direct benefits to people other than the employer or union.
scenes.label: Product Information
scenes.visual: Same three-step graphic remains on screen. Static composition with professional, muted color palette.

scenes.audio: Do not confuse employee group protection with a business owning key person insurance for its own financial loss.
scenes.label: Product Information
scenes.visual: Three-step graphic remains static. Palette focuses on teal, green, and cream tones.

scenes.audio: A trust can hold group coverage for participating employers or unions under Maryland's rules. The trust or trustees become the policyholder.
scenes.label: Product Information
scenes.visual: Transition to a new graphic title 'Other groups have their own legal structure'. A green box 'Trust group' appears on the left.

scenes.audio: A qualifying association can also sponsor coverage, but merely gathering names to buy insurance does not satisfy the association requirements.
scenes.label: Product Information
scenes.visual: A second green box 'Association' appears in the center of the frame. Minimalist styling consistent with previous graphics.

scenes.audio: A debtor group is different again. The creditor, or another authorized holder, insures eligible debtors in connection with their obligations.
scenes.label: Product Information
scenes.visual: A third dark teal box 'Debtor group' appears on the right. All three categories are now visible in a row.

scenes.audio: The payment addresses the insured debt, with any payable excess handled under the applicable rule. Identify the legal group and its purpose.
scenes.label: Product Information
scenes.visual: Static graphic of the three legal group types. High contrast between teal/green elements and the light background.

scenes.audio: An insurer evaluates the group's characteristics, eligibility rules, and participation. Stable membership and defined benefit classes can reduce chances of adverse selection.
scenes.label: Product Information
scenes.visual: New graphic: 'Group underwriting still manages selection'. A vertical list '01 Group profile' and '02 Eligibility' fades in.

scenes.audio: That is a selection issue, not a promise that no individual ever needs evidence of insurability.
scenes.label: Product Information
scenes.visual: The list adds '03 Enrollment' and '04 Evidence'. Static frame on the four underwriting pillars.

scenes.audio: A late entrant, or a person requesting an amount above a stated evidence-free limit, may face additional requirements under the actual plan.
scenes.label: Product Information
scenes.visual: Underwriting list remains static. The color scheme emphasizes professional trust with dark teals and light creams.

scenes.audio: Maryland also permits specified individual insurability exclusions or limits in these group statutes. Read the enrollment window carefully.
scenes.label: Product Information
scenes.visual: Final static view of the underwriting graphic before the next transition.

scenes.audio: If Elena contributes toward her insurance premium, the plan is contributory. If the employer pays the full premium, it is noncontributory.
scenes.label: Product Information
scenes.visual: Graphic: 'Funding and benefits answer different questions'. Three vertical columns: 'Contributory', 'Noncontributory', and 'Benefit recipient'.

scenes.audio: Maryland's employer rule generally covers all eligible employees in that noncontributory arrangement, subject to written rejections.
scenes.label: Product Information
scenes.visual: Funding graphic remains static. The 'Noncontributory' column is visually balanced with the 'Contributory' side.

scenes.audio: Funding alone does not make the employer the death beneficiary. Benefits ordinarily follow the insured's designation and policy provisions.
scenes.label: Product Information
scenes.visual: Funding graphic remains static. Focus transitions to the 'Benefit recipient' column.

scenes.audio: Eligible dependents may have separate coverage. A spouse listed only as beneficiary is not thereby an insured spouse.
scenes.label: Product Information
scenes.visual: Graphic remains static. Muted saturation levels for a professional instructional look.

scenes.audio: Marcus leaves covered employment. Under Maryland conversion, an eligible person applies and pays the first premium within 31 days.
scenes.label: Product Information
scenes.visual: Graphic: 'Conversion protects a limited opportunity'. Steps '01 Qualifying loss', '02 Apply and pay', and '03 Individual coverage' appear in sequence.

scenes.audio: New evidence of insurability is not required. The individual form, amount, and premium follow the statute and available contract terms.
scenes.label: Product Information
scenes.visual: Conversion steps graphic remains static. Sharp, high-contrast text for legibility.

scenes.audio: Conversion is different from portability. Ending the entire group policy also invokes a separate conversion provision. Revisit part 16 for limits.
scenes.label: Product Information
scenes.visual: Final view of the conversion graphic. Clean layout with ample white space.

scenes.audio: Federal Employees Group Life Insurance, or FEGLI, provides group term coverage for eligible federal employees.
scenes.label: Usage Scenarios
scenes.visual: Return to the office scene. The Hispanic woman, Black man, and blonde woman continue their discussion at the table. Same lighting and character appearances.

scenes.audio: Basic and elected optional coverage are provided. It does not build a cash value.
scenes.label: Product Information
scenes.visual: Graphic: 'Recognize the federal program names'. Three boxes appear: 'FEGLI', 'SGLI', and 'VGLI' with brief descriptions.

scenes.audio: SGLI provides term coverage to service members. VGLI can continue term protection after military service.
scenes.label: Product Information
scenes.visual: Federal programs graphic remains static. The palette uses teal, gold, and dark grey accents.

scenes.audio: These are different programs with their own deadlines. Use current government guidance. Do not replace federal rules with generic state deadlines.
scenes.label: Call to Action
scenes.visual: Static graphic of federal programs remains until the video end. Clean, branded aesthetic.
